title: Acceptance Criteria: Progressive Schema Tolerance, Tool Backpressure, and Post-Stream Reconciliation
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Define unambiguous acceptance criteria for progressive/lenient schema tolerance during streamed structured outputs, explicit backpressure signaling to upstream LLM runtimes and clients, and deterministic post-stream reconciliation for tool/function call semantics. Goal: make real-world partial emissions safe for tool handoff while keeping observability and testability for production rollouts.
background: Multiple customer reports and internal chaos in the past 6 months around tool double-invocation, partial JSON fragments, and opaque failures when streams are interrupted. Previous tickets cover handshake and fragmented envelopes; this ticket consolidates a pragmatic acceptance checklist that balances strict schema validation with graceful toleration and reconciliation flows required by production apps.
scope: Define envelope markers and checkpoint tokens for progressive emission (start/checkpoint/commit/abort)
Specify backpressure signal semantics (runtime -> client headers/frames and client -> runtime throttle hints)
Define idempotency contract for tool/function invocations tied to stream checkpoints
Define observable assertions and minimum telemetry for rollout gating
Define test harness and synthetic scenarios for interrupted streams and resume-with-checkpoint
out_of_scope: Full redesign of the tool gateway API (will be a follow-up if acceptance fails)
Large-scale cust-facing UX changes in Console (only telemetry/flags included)
New authentication or RBAC primitives (use existing KMS/Audit capabilities)
acceptance_criteria: Envelope markers: Every streamed structured-response must include deterministic start and commit markers and may include ordered checkpoint markers. Marker format defined as: "<<ENVELOPE v1|id:UUID|seq:n>>". Runtime must accept both v1 and legacy formats for 90 days after rollout.

Checkpoint semantics: Checkpoints create a durable, monotonic checkpoint-id that clients can reference to request a resume. Resume must guarantee no duplicate tool invocations for successfully checkpointed steps.

Tool invocation idempotency: Each tool/function call emitted in a stream must carry a tooling_id that is a stable hash of (user_request_id + stream_checkpoint_id + invocation_index). Runtime must never invoke the same tooling_id more than once unless the tool explicitly signals non-idempotency in its registration metadata.

Partial-object tolerance: Parsers should accept incremental fragments if envelope markers indicate a future commit. If a fragment cannot be reconciled into valid JSON by final commit, the runtime must emit a clearly typed error frame and trigger the reconciliation policy (retry/resume/abort).

Backpressure signaling: Runtime must expose a backpressure frame type with fields (allowed_rate_tokens_per_sec, recommended_batch_window_ms, current_queue_depth). Clients must honor backpressure within 2x for soft backpressure and within 100ms for hard backpressure frames.

Observable assertions: For every streaming session, the platform must emit telemetry covering: bytes_streamed, checkpoints_committed, tool_invocations_attempted, tool_invocations_succeeded, duplicate_tool_invocation_count, backpressure_events, final_commit_status. These metrics must be available in Console within 10 minutes of session termination.

Failure modes and recovery: If connection drops after commit X but before commit X+1, client may resume from commit X. Resume must not re-run invocations that were acked by the tool gateway; plumbing must rely on tooling_id for deduplication. If a resume is impossible (missing checkpoint) the runtime must expose a replay token and a deterministic fallback model variant per policy.

Test harness: Provide automated tests that simulate TCP drop, server crash, and client reconnects. Acceptance requires zero duplicate positive-side effects in 1000 synthetic runs for each scenario and duplicate_tool_invocation_count <= 0.1% across runs.

Schema evolution tolerance: When an emitter upgrades schema (new optional fields), older clients must be able to parse at runtime without failing provided envelope version remains compatible. Platform should expose a schema-compatibility-report per model variant.

Error classification: All stream-level errors must be typed as: transient | recoverable | fatal. Recoverable errors must surface guidance and replay tokens; fatal errors must include failure_code and human_readable_hint. Console error drill-down must link to the replay token and relevant checkpoints.
Security: Any checkpoint tokens or replay tokens must be short-lived (TTL <= 1 hour) and recorded in Audit logs along with originating request_id and user_identity.

Rollout gating: Feature rollouts must be behind a kill-switch flag per-customer and require observability pass: duplicate_tool_invocation_rate < 0.5% and mean time-to-detect-replay-issues < 15 minutes in Canary traffic before widening rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope marker parsing, checkpoint generation, and tooling_id deterministic hashing
Integration test that wires a mock tool gateway; simulate stream commit, crash, resume and assert no double-exec
Chaos experiment: randomly drop network and restart runtime; assert telemetry signals and replay flow behave within SLOs
Load test: verify backpressure frames throttle clients and end-to-end latency stays within configured SLOs under burst load
Security test: attempt to reuse expired replay token and verify rejection with proper audit log entry
dependencies: ENG-31001 (console: streaming telemetry ingestion and dashboards)
risks: Overly strict schema enforcement could break many customers who rely on progressive emissions
Idempotency guarantees rely on tool gateway cooperation; third-party tools that ignore tooling_id may cause duplicates
Increased telemetry retention and ingestion cost for high-volume streams
notes: 2025-02-11: Initial scoping meeting with runtime, SDK, and tool-gateway leads. Consensus on envelope marker prototype.
2025-02-13: Design suggested using UUIDv7 for checkpoint IDs to encode time for TTL enforcement.
2025-02-16: Engineering proposes a soft launch via canary flag and per-tenant kill switches.
Review feedback (2025-02-17): Security asked to shorten replay token TTL to 1 hour and add explicit audit entries. Added to acceptance criteria.
open_questions: What retention window for checkpoints is acceptable for large-enterprise customers who need multi-day resumes? (proposal: enterprise opt-in extendable via contract)
Do we expose a client SDK helper to automatically honor backpressure frames, or rely on partner SDKs to implement logic?
Should non-idempotent tools be blocked by default from being invoked in streamed contexts?
